findings.text: The first lines tell a newcomer what Athena is and what makes it different. A reader can say what the site is about without scrolling.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The header explains why the page exists and why it matters: it shows that Athena's output can be traced back to source. The footer and the claim links back this up, because each claim links to file lines at the pinned commit.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: A next step is offered early and links to a concrete Next steps section. That section has the repo link, an install command and a sample command, so the reader knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The install steps say nothing about prerequisites (for example the Rust toolchain or AI model access/keys). They also don't say that `athena ask` must be run inside a target git repository, so a newcomer may get stuck at the first try.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: The Start here section and its up-front definitions of captain, yolo, green and red help a newcomer read the rest. It is also honest about gaps, for example that "in scope" is not defined by the source.
Several terms are used but never defined, even though the glossary is long: "captain call", "wake", "heartbeat" and "endpoint". A newcomer has to guess what they mean.
findings.source: "Teardown finds the backlog item is still an open captain call"; "A stale wake shows the worker is stuck"; "after every teardown and heartbeat"

findings.text: "Ship" is a core task kind, but its glossary definition is circular and vague. The clearer meaning ("A ship changes a project") appears only in the "What firstmate is" list.
findings.source: Glossary entry "ship": "A kind of task, named next to scouts."

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed state machine of firstmate, with 11 transition cards and 44 claims. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets the point after the header and Start here, and the rest is reference-level detail they will probably skim.
